key_insight: OmniQEC uses an LLM-driven slow-and-fast search loop to discover quantum error-correcting codes that are not only good on paper, but also workable under circuit-level and decoder-level constraints.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets practical fault-tolerant quantum hardware by co-designing the code, syndrome extraction, and decoding to improve deployable logical error suppression.
method: LLM orchestrator generates and iteratively refines QEC candidates
Fast loop screens codes with inexpensive code-level proxies
Slow loop evaluates physically grounded syndrome-extraction circuits and decoder performance, then feeds results back into search
evidence_signal: Across four qLDPC families and three LLM backends, the discovered codes improved with larger physical-qubit budgets and beat BB codes with [![72,12,6!]] and [![144,12,12!]] at complete-implementation budgets of 98 and 240 physical qubits.
watch_item: Performance depends on the chosen hardware, syndrome-extraction synthesis, and decoder quality, so gains may not transfer uniformly across architectures or implementation constraints.
paper_title: OmniQEC: discovering practical quantum error-correcting codes by an AI scientist
